pr.body:
## Summary This pull request introduces a new feature to manage calendar cache data, including the ability to view cache status and delete cached data. It also includes several supporting updates to repositories, APIs, and UI components. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme. ### New Feature: Calendar Cache Management * Added a `deleteCache` mutation to the TRPC `calendarsRouter`, enabling users to delete cached calendar data by credential ID. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsxR27-R33](diffhunk://#diff-9e053175cc6dfb5717313e0587a730fff132f9d3c1200204f0ce8dac53a19280R27-R33)`) * Introduced the `deleteCacheHandler` to handle cache deletion logic, including validation of user access to the specified credential. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.tsR1-R33](diffhunk://#diff-572888b8e0555167a5787847f29d5a46623eff170491acc0654e916f5b4afd18R1-R33)`) * Updated the `connectedCalendarsHandler` to enrich calendar data with cache status (`cacheUpdatedAt`) by querying the `CalendarCacheRepository`. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.tsR27-R39](diffhunk://#diff-3f6a556ad60f26d0162770fcd81b5bddeb6ab0437552ac792045c3cd2608d710R27-R39)`) ### UI Enhancements * Created a new `CredentialActionsDropdown` component to display cache status and provide options to delete cached data or disconnect integrations. (`[packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsxR1-R134](diffhunk://#diff-c78273434b95ab8276bb5eb24d9bc088b10af029388bdcd08cbe478f44269b31R1-R134)`) * Replaced the `DisconnectIntegration` component with `CredentialActionsDropdown` in the `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` UI, integrating the new cache management functionality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L5-R5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L70-L81)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L125-L135)`) ### Repository and Database Updates * Added a `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method to the `CalendarCacheRepository` and its mock implementation to fetch cache statuses for multiple credentials. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b36c72c0db751ba0cafe234dfa150817672869825333c22b074c4977a6135b8dR30-R32)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ceffbae9ef3da413495feac73a341672e77ffaf493cf67ada0b637ead80ded38R26-R30)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4cf8d3089fad7b6c8fe4172d8d42147f136b65baf30b726e57b9b10d179d4a99R172-R188)`) * Introduced a new `updateManyByCredentialId` method in the `SelectedCalendarRepository` to update multiple calendars by credential ID. (`[packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.tsR400-R406](diffhunk://#diff-ccb4eecfa701e5b0c7d6ba87dcc550cdf3700a63ee252849045611599ecb9273R400-R406)`) * Added an `updatedAt` column to the `CalendarCache` table in the database schema and Prisma model to track the last update timestamp. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f597bd98bbcfdcf4861ee7bf0c238e7dfe54b456ceb69b852aaf3979c4102cfR1-R8)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-56fa4d384ba6fb94b130e9eb42c5cad00734b025ebd6c197f76873469725ae87R1718)`) ### Localization and Strings * Added new localization strings for cache management actions, such as "Cache Status," "Delete cached data," and "Cache deleted successfully." (`[apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.jsonR3376-R3382](diffhunk://#diff-57de4b8e5231f1d699891d98b0381d56e9e24537b0ca5420d1fba4f0597370bcR3376-R3382)`) ### Miscellaneous * Updated `package.json` to replace `ts-node` with `npx tsx` for running the `dev:cron` script. (`[apps/web/package.jsonL11-R11](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8L11-R11)`) ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human **🔴 High Priority (5 items)** - [x] **Verify deleteCache tRPC mutation exists** - The component references `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache.useMutation()` but this mutation implementation is not visible in the PR changes. Check if this endpoint exists or needs to be created. - [x] **End-to-end testing with Google Calendar** - Install a Google Calendar integration and verify the credential-level dropdown appears, shows cache status, and deletion flow works correctly with confirmation dialog. - [x] **Test cache status display logic** - Verify that `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamps are correctly formatted and displayed only for Google Calendar credentials with actual cache data. - [x] **Confirm repository pattern correctness** - Test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` returns accurate data and the credential-to-cache mapping works properly in the UI. - [x] **Verify dropdown conditional rendering** - Ensure the dropdown only appears for Google Calendar credentials and handles edge cases (no cache, disabled integrations, etc.). **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Connect a Google Calendar integration to trigger cache creation 2. Navigate to `/apps/installed/calendar` 3. Verify dropdown appears on Google Calendar credential with cache status and timestamp 4. Test "Delete cached data" action shows confirmation dialog 5. Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately 6. Test "Remove App" functionality still works correctly --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD UI["CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx
(New Component)"]:::major-edit Handler["connectedCalendars.handler.ts
(Updated tRPC Handler)"]:::major-edit RepoInterface["calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts
(Updated Interface)"]:::minor-edit RepoImpl["calendar-cache.repository.ts
(Updated Implementation)"]:::minor-edit RepoMock["calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts
(Updated Mock)"]:::minor-edit Translations["common.json
(Added Translation Keys)"]:::minor-edit UI -->|"Uses repository via tRPC"| Handler Handler -->|"Calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds"| RepoImpl RepoImpl -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface RepoMock -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface UI -->|"Uses translation keys"| Translations subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - **Session Details**: Requested by @zomars, implemented in Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/24545e0980df465995521419432a2a52 - **SelectedCalendar.updatedAt Usage**: Currently only updated in backend via Google webhook handler but not displayed in frontend. Frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache. Consider if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update should be removed. - **Import Path Resolution**: Had to fix UI component import paths during development - watch for potential module resolution issues in different environments. - **Testing Limitation**: Local testing was limited due to no installed calendar integrations - end-to-end verification with real Google Calendar data is essential.

raw_findings.root_cause: A shared cleanup function unconditionally exits successfully regardless of why it was invoked.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Let `cleanup` accept and preserve an exit status, calling it with a nonzero code on failure and zero only for normal signal/cleanup paths.
raw_findings.title: Failure paths exit with a successful status
raw_findings.trigger: Tunnelmole is rate-limited, fails to start, or no tunnel URL can be extracted and the script calls `cleanup`.

raw_findings.body: The helper either fails to obtain a URL or writes a stale tunnel URL to `.env`, despite claiming to reuse the currently running process.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The configured webhook points to no tunnel or to the wrong tunnel.
raw_findings.impact: The helper either fails to obtain a URL or writes a stale tunnel URL to `.env`, despite claiming to reuse the currently running process.
raw_findings.root_cause: Process detection and URL discovery use independent sources with no guarantee that the fixed log belongs to the detected process.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only reuse a process when its PID and URL were recorded together by this script, otherwise start a new tunnel or obtain the active URL from Tunnelmole itself.
raw_findings.title: Reusing an existing tunnel assumes an unrelated fixed log file contains its URL
raw_findings.trigger: A `tmole 3000` process was started outside this script, or `/tmp/tmole.log` contains output from an older tunnel.

raw_findings.body: The script exits immediately instead of waiting, so the user has no opportunity to press Ctrl+C as instructed and cannot stop the reused process through this helper.
raw_findings.evidence: echo "Tunnelmole is running. Press Ctrl+C to stop."
raw_findings.failure_mode: CLI documentation misstates the script's actual lifecycle and control behavior.
raw_findings.impact: The script exits immediately instead of waiting, so the user has no opportunity to press Ctrl+C as instructed and cannot stop the reused process through this helper.
raw_findings.root_cause: An unconditional status message describes only the newly started-tunnel branch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Print the Ctrl+C instruction only when this script owns and waits for the tunnel; otherwise state that the existing tunnel was reused and the helper is exiting.
raw_findings.title: The final status message is false when an existing tunnel is reused
raw_findings.trigger: The script detects and reuses an existing Tunnelmole process, setting `OWNED_PID=false`.

finding.body: The route still queries the real cache table and can expose cache actions even though the established `CalendarCache.init` path would select `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` and suppress the feature.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.880 is below 0.920: Line 28 shows `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instantiated directly, bypassing CalendarCache.init() which checks the calendar-cache feature flag. finding.body: Every legacy row receives the deployment timestamp, so old or expired cache data is displayed as having been updated when the migration ran rather than when the cache was actually written.
finding.evidence: ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();
finding.failure_mode: The newly displayed “Last updated” value is fabricated for legacy cache entries.
finding.impact: Every legacy row receives the deployment timestamp, so old or expired cache data is displayed as having been updated when the migration ran rather than when the cache was actually written.
finding.root_cause: The migration uses the current migration time as historical freshness data for all existing rows.
finding.suggested_fix: Backfill from reliable existing write metadata, or leave legacy values null and make the field nullable until a real cache write supplies a timestamp.
finding.title: Legacy cache rows are falsely marked as updated at migration time
finding.trigger: The migration runs against a non-empty `CalendarCache` table and the new status UI reads those existing rows.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 9 shows `DEFAULT NOW()` which sets all existing rows to migration timestamp. This is factually accurate - legacy cache entries will show the migration time as their updatedAt, not their actual cache write time.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.900 is below 0.920: Line 9 shows `DEFAULT NOW()` which sets all existing rows to migration timestamp. This is factually accurate - legacy cache entries will show the migration time as their updatedAt, not their actual cache write time.

finding.body: The cached query continues supplying the old `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the UI still shows cache status and the delete action after the server has deleted the rows.
finding.failure_mode: Client-side TRPC state remains stale after a successful destructive mutation.
finding.impact: The cached query continues supplying the old `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the UI still shows cache status and the delete action after the server has deleted the rows.
finding.root_cause: The new mutation delegates refresh behavior to an optional callback instead of invalidating the query that owns the displayed state.
finding.suggested_fix: Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the delete mutation's `onSuccess` or `onSettled`, independently of the optional callback.
finding.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query
finding.trigger: A user deletes cached data where `onSuccess` is absent or does not explicitly refetch `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, such as a wrapper invocation without an `onChanged` callback.
finding.verifier_reason: The disconnectMutation at lines 53-65 includes onSettled which calls utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(). The deleteCacheMutation only calls onSuccess callback, but the claim about stale cache after delete is about deleteCacheMutation, not disconnect. However, callers pass onChanged which typically refetches.

rejected_findings.reason: The disconnectMutation at lines 53-65 includes onSettled which calls utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(). The deleteCacheMutation only calls onSuccess callback, but the claim about stale cache after delete is about deleteCacheMutation, not disconnect. finding.body: tRPC classifies the generic exception as an internal error rather than an expected not-found or forbidden response, producing incorrect API status and noisy server-error reporting.

finding.suggested_fix: Throw a `TRPCError` with a deliberate `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN` code while retaining a non-enumerating message if desired.

finding.trigger: A caller supplies a nonexistent credential ID or an ID belonging to another user.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 25 throws generic `new Error()` instead of TRPCError. tRPC will convert this to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than appropriate NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN status codes.

validated_findings.body: Invalid database identifiers pass API validation and reach Prisma or the generic not-found branch, yielding a misleading server error instead of a validation response.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Malformed identifiers are accepted beyond the API boundary.
validated_findings.impact: Invalid database identifiers pass API validation and reach Prisma or the generic not-found branch, yielding a misleading server error instead of a validation response.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new mutation validates only the JavaScript number type, not the constraints of the database identifier.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Validate with `z.number().int().positive()` or reuse a shared credential-ID schema.
validated_findings.title: Credential IDs are not constrained to valid integer identifiers
validated_findings.trigger: A client submits a fractional, zero, or negative number as `credentialId`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 29 shows `z.number()` validation which accepts any JavaScript number including negatives, zero, and floats. Database credential IDs are positive integers, so invalid values pass validation.

validated_findings.body: The patch adds a user-authorized destructive endpoint without tests proving that owned cache rows are deleted and foreign credentials are rejected, so an access-control or over-deletion regression can merge undetected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Review and CI cannot verify the endpoint's core security and data-isolation contract.
validated_findings.impact: The patch adds a user-authorized destructive endpoint without tests proving that owned cache rows are deleted and foreign credentials are rejected, so an access-control or over-deletion regression can merge undetected.
validated_findings.root_cause: No automated tests accompany the new ownership check and credential-scoped delete operation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add handler/router tests covering successful deletion for an owned credential, rejection for another user's credential, nonexistent IDs, and preservation of unrelated cache rows.
validated_findings.title: The destructive authorization boundary has no regression tests
validated_findings.trigger: The ownership predicate or deletion query is later modified, or the handler receives another user's credential ID.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test gap findings are process/coverage observations, not defects introduced by the patch. The authorization logic at lines 17-22 is straightforward and the absence of tests doesn't constitute a bug in the code itself.

validated_findings.body: `npx` resolves and downloads an uncontrolled package version from the registry, making the script nondeterministic and causing it to fail when registry access is unavailable.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A repository script depends on network availability and whichever package version is current at invocation time.
validated_findings.impact: `npx` resolves and downloads an uncontrolled package version from the registry, making the script nondeterministic and causing it to fail when registry access is unavailable.
validated_findings.root_cause: The package script relies on `npx` fallback installation instead of a lockfile-managed dependency.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a pinned `tsx` development dependency through Yarn and invoke the workspace binary directly, for example `tsx cron-tester.ts` or `yarn tsx cron-tester.ts`.
validated_findings.title: The cron script now downloads an unpinned runner at execution time
validated_findings.trigger: A developer runs `dev:cron` without `tsx` already available in the workspace, especially offline or after a new `tsx` release.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Using npx tsx is a common pattern in monorepos. The tsx package is widely used and npx caches packages locally. This is a stylistic preference, not a bug - the script will work correctly.

validated_findings.body: The script edits or creates `.env` one directory above the repository instead of the repository's environment file, while still reporting success.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The webhook URL is written to the wrong file and the application does not receive the configuration.
validated_findings.impact: The script edits or creates `.env` one directory above the repository instead of the repository's environment file, while still reporting success.
validated_findings.root_cause: A repository file path is based on the process working directory rather than the script's own location.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the repository root from the script location, such as `SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)` and `ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env"`.
validated_findings.title: The webhook helper resolves `.env` relative to the caller's directory
validated_findings.trigger: The executable is invoked conventionally from the repository root as `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, or from any directory other than `scripts`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 5 shows `ENV_FILE="../.env"` which is relative to current working directory, not script location. Running from repo root as `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` would resolve to parent directory's .env.

validated_findings.body: GNU `sed` interprets the empty argument differently and the replacement command fails, so the existing webhook URL is not updated.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The helper fails on a common supported development platform precisely when replacing an existing value.
validated_findings.impact: GNU `sed` interprets the empty argument differently and the replacement command fails, so the existing webhook URL is not updated.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new cross-platform shell script hardcodes BSD/macOS in-place editing syntax.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use a portable temporary-file replacement or branch between GNU `sed -i -E` and BSD `sed -i '' -E`.
validated_findings.title: The environment update uses macOS-only `sed -i` syntax
validated_findings.trigger: The script runs on GNU/Linux and the environment file already contains `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 68 shows `sed -i '' -E` which is BSD/macOS syntax. GNU sed requires `sed -i -E` (no empty string argument). This will fail on Linux systems.

validated_findings.body: The script prints a failure but returns status 0, so calling scripts, terminals, and automation treat the setup as successful.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Operational failures cannot be detected from the process exit code.
validated_findings.impact: The script prints a failure but returns status 0, so calling scripts, terminals, and automation treat the setup as successful.
validated_findings.root_cause: A shared cleanup function unconditionally exits successfully regardless of why it was invoked.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Let `cleanup` accept and preserve an exit status, calling it with a nonzero code on failure and zero only for normal signal/cleanup paths.
validated_findings.title: Failure paths exit with a successful status
validated_findings.trigger: Tunnelmole is rate-limited, fails to start, or no tunnel URL can be extracted and the script calls `cleanup`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 17 shows `exit 0` in cleanup function called on failure paths (line 58). When tunnel URL extraction fails, cleanup is called but exits with success status 0.

validated_findings.body: The helper either fails to obtain a URL or writes a stale tunnel URL to `.env`, despite claiming to reuse the currently running process.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The configured webhook points to no tunnel or to the wrong tunnel.
validated_findings.impact: The helper either fails to obtain a URL or writes a stale tunnel URL to `.env`, despite claiming to reuse the currently running process.
validated_findings.root_cause: Process detection and URL discovery use independent sources with no guarantee that the fixed log belongs to the detected process.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Only reuse a process when its PID and URL were recorded together by this script, otherwise start a new tunnel or obtain the active URL from Tunnelmole itself.
validated_findings.title: Reusing an existing tunnel assumes an unrelated fixed log file contains its URL
validated_findings.trigger: A `tmole 3000` process was started outside this script, or `/tmp/tmole.log` contains output from an older tunnel.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 28-30 show reuse path reads from fixed LOG_FILE which may contain stale URL from previous tunnel session. No verification that the detected process wrote to this specific log file.

validated_findings.body: The script exits immediately instead of waiting, so the user has no opportunity to press Ctrl+C as instructed and cannot stop the reused process through this helper.
validated_findings.evidence: echo "Tunnelmole is running. Press Ctrl+C to stop."
validated_findings.failure_mode: CLI documentation misstates the script's actual lifecycle and control behavior.
validated_findings.impact: The script exits immediately instead of waiting, so the user has no opportunity to press Ctrl+C as instructed and cannot stop the reused process through this helper.
validated_findings.root_cause: An unconditional status message describes only the newly started-tunnel branch.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Print the Ctrl+C instruction only when this script owns and waits for the tunnel; otherwise state that the existing tunnel was reused and the helper is exiting.
validated_findings.title: The final status message is false when an existing tunnel is reused
validated_findings.trigger: The script detects and reuses an existing Tunnelmole process, setting `OWNED_PID=false`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 74 prints 'Press Ctrl+C to stop' but when OWNED_PID=false (reuse path), script exits immediately at line 77-79 without waiting. The message is misleading for the reuse case.
